facts.F214: Owner: Portfolio (Models/Portfolio.cs) owns the starting value of Default Feature sizing. The property InfersDefaultFeatureSize starts false (off). A new method Portfolio.StartOnConnection(connection) assigns the connection and sets the switch on exactly when the connection names a Portfolio Size Estimate Field default (SizeEstimateFieldForPortfolios has a value), else leaves it off. It is a named method, not a property setter, so EF materialisation of a stored row never runs it. Only the create path calls it, once, before SyncWithPortfolioSettings. Existing rows are never rewritten; a connection default set after a Portfolio exists does not switch it on.
facts.F215: EF mapping: no migration. Mapping stays HasDefaultValue(true).HasSentinel(true). Table, entity value then stored result: CLR false (absent field, no connection default, or explicit false) differs from the sentinel, so EF inserts false (off). CLR true (rule with a connection default, or explicit true) equals the sentinel, EF omits the column, the DB default true applies (on). Both starting values store correctly. Existing rows and restored old backups hold true and are not touched. Changing the DB column default is rejected: it needs an expand-only migration for every provider and changes no observable outcome.
facts.F216: Create path: PortfoliosController.CreatePortfolio calls newPortfolio.StartOnConnection(connection) where it now assigns the connection, before the setting-refusal check and SyncWithPortfolioSettings. PortfolioExtensions keeps the entity value when the DTO bool? is null, so an absent field gives the rule value and a named true or false wins. The create wizard omits infersDefaultFeatureSize from its settings, so the backend is the single owner of the starting value (the type already allows an absent field). Clone sends the source settings, so it keeps the source value. The frontend read fallback stays true: it only meets stored values or the missing field of an older server, and both mean on. Usage event 29 does not fire on a wizard create, because an omitted field reads as on and nothing switches on to off.
facts.F217: Demo data: DemoDataFactory builds demo Portfolios off (entity default). DemoDataService assigns the demo connection afterwards, and that connection names no Portfolio Size Estimate Field default, so the rule would also give off: the demo path needs no call to StartOnConnection today. If a demo connection ever names such a default, DemoDataService must call StartOnConnection instead of assigning the connection. A demo Portfolio gets InfersDefaultFeatureSize = true in DemoDataFactory only where a measured screenshot result needs inferred sizes; the crafter runs each affected @screenshot test alone and decides per Portfolio.
facts.F218: Test port: create has no application service; the controller builds the Portfolio. The lowest layer that proves the starting value is PortfoliosController.CreatePortfolio over real SQLite EF, as NewPortfolioStartingValueTest already does through ServicePortHarness; its table gains rows for a connection naming a size field default by absent, explicit false and explicit true. The wizard test pins that the settings sent omit the field. The five Slice10 PortfoliosSizeEstimateFieldDefault scenarios run unchanged and must go green. The older-client wire concern stays in PortfolioSettingDtoCompatibilityTest (connection without a default). No web host start is warranted for the new rows.
facts.F219: Patterns: chosen, a domain-owned named method on the aggregate (Portfolio.StartOnConnection) over a constructor-level false default alone: one owner, called by the one create path, testable without a host. Rejected: an if in the controller (rule outside the entity); a setter on the connection property that sets the switch (EF materialisation would flip stored rows); wizard derives the value from the connection (second owner, races a later connection change); set false in the controller and demo factory (two owners); change the DB column default (migration, no gain); heuristic migration for already using it (maintainer rejected, moves forecasts); nullable stored value as a third state (needs migration and a resolver).
